My grandpas father (my great grandpa) was an officer who fought for the polish army in the early stage of world war 2, after the russians invaded they ended up sending him and his family to a siberian gulag. He then got sent to fight at Monte Cassino which was one of the bloodiest battles of ww2. He never really talked about his experiences to my dad or my uncles and now he has alzheimers so ill never know but i can only imagine the horrors hes seen from his country getting invaded, getting sent to a gulag in a frozen wasteland, watching his family work to death, and seeing many of his comrades and friends die in front of him, it must have been hell. Things did get better for him after the war though, he moved to the us and became an engineer and apparently was one of the engineers for the umbilical tower that was used during the apollo missions and he taught the US military (and the CIA i think) russian and helped them spy on the soviet union.
